course.description.source: Discover how different communities express their beliefs, identities, work and power through art and architecture. Explore real objects, paintings, homes, streets and heritage traditions in Southeast Asia and around the world, and learn how cultural ideas change and travel.
course.description.back: Discover how different communities express belief, identity, work and power through art and architecture. Explore real objects, paintings, houses, streets and traditions that are heritage in Southeast Asia and around the world, then learn how cultural ideas change and travel to different places.

sections.0.question.source: How do an object's form, materials and makers connect it to a society?
sections.0.question.back: How do the form, materials and makers of one object connect that object to society?

sections.0.description.source: Study a Japanese print, a Flemish painting, Javanese batik, Vietnamese and Chinese objects, art made for rulers in Egypt and Peru, and a Mughal court album, and see how making, work, exchange and patronage shape what people create.
sections.0.description.note: Names: Flemish painting ภาพวาดเฟลมิช, Javanese batik ผ้าบาติกชวา, Mughal court album อัลบั้มภาพของราชสำนักโมกุล, Peru เปรู. Check. Reviewer: fixed งานศิลปะที่ทำให้ผู้ปกครอง (read as 'art that made rulers ...', unfinished) to ที่ทำขึ้นเพื่อผู้ปกครอง ('made for rulers').
sections.0.description.back: Study Japanese prints, Flemish paintings, Javanese batik cloth, objects from Vietnam and China, artworks made for rulers in Egypt and Peru, and a picture album of the Mughal court, then see how making, work, exchange and patronage affect what people create.

sections.1.question.source: How do buildings and landscapes express a community's beliefs, authority and everyday life?
sections.1.question.back: How do buildings and landscapes show a community's beliefs, power and daily life?

sections.1.description.source: Explore Toraja houses, Borobudur, Angkor Wat, the trading streets of George Town and Amsterdam, and the Ifugao rice terraces, and see how people organise space around belief, power, work and the land.
sections.1.description.note: Names: Toraja บ้านของชาวโตราจา, George Town จอร์จทาวน์, Amsterdam อัมสเตอร์ดัม, Ifugao rice terraces นาขั้นบันไดของชาวอีฟูเกา. Check against the lessons' translators.
sections.1.description.back: Explore Toraja houses, Borobudur, Angkor Wat, the trading streets of George Town and Amsterdam, and the Ifugao rice terraces, then see how people arrange space according to belief, power, work and the land.

sections.2.title.note: KEY_TERMS marks เรื่องเล่า ชีวิต และความทรงจำของสังคม (check); used as given.

sections.2.question.source: How do images and monuments tell stories, show work and shape what people remember?
sections.2.question.back: How do pictures and monuments tell stories, show work, and shape what people remember?

sections.2.description.source: Read Thai Buddhist paintings, French pictures of rural work and a changing modern world, Rodin's monument to Calais, and two paintings of Prince Diponegoro's arrest, and ask who gets to picture history.
sections.2.description.note: Rodin and Diponegoro kept in Latin letters (people's names, as in AAS14, AAS15, AAS20); Calais เมืองกาแล; 'Thai Buddhist paintings' จิตรกรรมพุทธศาสนาของไทย. 'who gets to picture history' rendered ใครได้เป็นผู้วาดภาพประวัติศาสตร์.
sections.2.description.back: Read Thai Buddhist paintings, French paintings about rural work and a modern world that is changing, Rodin's monument for the town of Calais, and two paintings about the arrest of Prince Diponegoro, then ask who got to be the one who paints history.

sections.3.question.source: How do museums, conservation and living traditions change what a work means?
sections.3.question.back: How do museums, conservation and living traditions change the meaning of a work?

sections.3.description.source: Follow Buddhist objects into museums, the Great Mosque of Djenné and the yearly work that keeps it standing, blue-and-white ceramics across Asia, and Mexico's Day of the Dead, then tell a fuller story about a work.
sections.3.description.note: Great Mosque of Djenné มัสยิดใหญ่แห่งเจนเน (as in AAS17); blue-and-white ceramics เครื่องลายครามสีน้ำเงินขาว (AAS18); Day of the Dead วันแห่งความตาย (AAS19). Reviewer: 'the yearly work that keeps it standing' was งานประจำปี (an annual fair or festival); changed to การซ่อมแซมทุกปี (the repairs done every year). Check it fits AAS17's wording for the replastering.
sections.3.description.back: Follow Buddhist objects that went into museums, the Great Mosque of Djenné and the repairs done every year that keep the mosque standing, blue-and-white porcelain across Asia, and Mexico's Day of the Dead, then tell a work's story more fully.

practiceOptions.3.source: I practised another way (quietly, with sign, or in writing)
practiceOptions.3.back: I practised another way (quietly, with sign language, or in writing)
